signature.name: VTask.prodMap
signature.type: {R : Type u} -> {M : Type v} -> {M₂ : Type w} -> {M₃ : Type y} -> {M₄ : Type z} -> [Semiring R] -> [AddCommMonoid M] -> [AddCommMonoid M₂] -> [AddCommMonoid M₃] -> [AddCommMonoid M₄] -> [Module R M] -> [Module R M₂] -> [Module R M₃] -> [Module R M₄] -> (f : M →ₗ[R] M₃) -> (g : M₂ →ₗ[R] M₄) -> M × M₂ →ₗ[R] M₃ × M₄

conventions.note: NONE_DECLARED: VTask.prodMap is a total construction on linear maps with no junk-value conventions; every pair of linear maps yields a well-defined linear map on the product.

facts.statement: ∀ (R : Type*) (M M₂ M₃ M₄ : Type*) [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [AddCommMonoid M₂] [AddCommMonoid M₃] [AddCommMonoid M₄] [Module R M] [Module R M₂] [Module R M₃] [Module R M₄] (f : M →ₗ[R] M₃) (g : M₂ →ₗ[R] M₄) (x y : M × M₂), VTask.prodMap f g (x + y) = VTask.prodMap f g x + VTask.prodMap f g y

facts.violated_property: The result should apply f to the first component and g to the second; swapping them gives a different map when f ≠ g
